name: Add Interactivity
description: Learn JavaScript by adding real interactivity to your web pages.

introduction.title: Make it Interactive with JavaScript
introduction.description: JavaScript is the programming language of the web. It allows you to make your site do things when users click, type, or scroll.

examples.title: Showing an Alert
examples.explanation: This pops up a message in the browser.

examples.title: Changing Content
examples.explanation: This finds the first <h1> and changes its text.

lessons.title: Variables & Output
lessons.description: Store data in variables and print it to the console.

challenges.title: Declare your first variables
challenges.description: Variables are labelled boxes that hold data — const for values that won't change, let for ones that will.
challenges.instructions: Declare a const called name with the value 'Jane Smith', and a let called age with the value 25.
challenges.starterCode:
// Variables store data

learn.heading: Variables
paragraphs: Variables hold data. Use `const` for values that won't change and `let` for values that can change.

learn.heading: Further Reading
paragraphs: Read MDN's JavaScript guide for a concise overview of variables and types.

textbook.title: MDN JavaScript Guide
textbook.excerpt: MDN's guide covers core JavaScript concepts with examples.

questions.prompt: Which keyword declares a variable whose value cannot be reassigned?

challenges.title: Log to the console
challenges.description: console.log prints values so you can see exactly what your code is doing.
challenges.instructions: Use console.log to print the name variable, then on a new line log the age variable.

learn.heading: Console Output
paragraphs: `console.log` prints values to the browser console. It's useful for debugging and seeing program output.

questions.prompt: What function prints values to the browser console?

challenges.title: Use a template literal
challenges.description: Template literals (backtick strings) let you embed variables directly inside a string using ${} syntax.
challenges.instructions: Use console.log with a template literal (backtick string) to print: Hello, Jane Smith! You are 25 years old. — using your name and age variables inside ${}.

learn.heading: Template Literals
paragraphs: Template literals use backticks and `${}` to embed expressions directly into strings.

questions.prompt: Which characters start a template literal in JavaScript?

lessons.title: Functions & Logic
lessons.description: Write reusable functions and make decisions with if/else.

challenges.title: Write a greeting function
challenges.description: Functions bundle code into a named, reusable block you can call any time.
challenges.instructions: Write a function called greet that takes a parameter called name and returns the string 'Hello, ' + name + '!'

challenges.title: Add an if/else check
challenges.description: if/else lets your code take different paths based on a condition.
challenges.instructions: Write a function called checkAge that takes a parameter age. If age is 18 or more, return the string 'adult'. Otherwise return 'minor'.

challenges.title: Call your functions
challenges.description: A function only runs when you call it. Put yours to work and log the results!
challenges.instructions: Call greet() passing in the name variable, and call checkAge() passing in the age variable. Log both return values with console.log.

lessons.title: DOM & Events
lessons.description: Use JavaScript to select page elements and respond to user actions in real time.

challenges.title: Grab an element and change its text
challenges.description: document.getElementById finds any element on the page by its id attribute.
challenges.instructions: Use document.getElementById('title') to get the h1 element and store it in a variable called titleEl. Then set titleEl.textContent to 'Welcome to my Portfolio!'.
challenges.starterCode:
// The page has:

,
hints:
const titleEl = document.getElementById('title');
titleEl.textContent = 'Welcome to my Portfolio!';

challenges.title: Listen for a click
challenges.description: addEventListener makes your page respond to user actions like button clicks.
challenges.instructions: Get the button (id='btn') and output paragraph (id='output'). Add a 'click' event listener to the button. Inside the handler, set output.textContent to 'Button clicked!'.

challenges.title: Count the clicks
challenges.description: Combine a variable with a template literal to track and display dynamic data on every click.
challenges.instructions: Declare a let count = 0 variable. Add a click event listener to the button. Inside the handler, increment count with count++ then set output.textContent to a template literal: 'You clicked X times!' using count.
